solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A verger no longer working as a servant of the Queen

indicators.note: working here means operating in a new way, so the letters of these words are put to work in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A church verger who has retired goes on to serve the monarch in some other capacity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' turns the fifteen letters of A VERGER NO LONGER into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The monarch's representative in a Commonwealth realm is formally appointed by and serves the Crown.

clue.text: Travel to Sweden, getting drinks and chats

parts.note: to go is to travel
S is the international vehicle code for Sweden
sips are small drinks

explanation.surface: A trip to Sweden involving drinks and conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle talk or chats about others are gossips, used as a verb or plural noun.

clue.text: Servant giving farewell ahead of time

indicators.note: ahead of places the farewell before the time in the down entry

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell

explanation.surface: A servant saying goodbye before it is time.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentleman's personal attendant is a manservant.

clue.text: Bird in reeds brat disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters of these words are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A bird nesting in reeds is upset by a naughty child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges REEDS BRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin is a familiar garden bird, often named for its red chest.

clue.text: Love to be given rest, ending with ugly fatness

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O
the infinitive phrase to be loses its 'to', leaving the verb be itself
to sit is to rest

indicators.note: ending with picks only the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Romance given a break, finishing with an unattractive paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Being severely overweight is a medical sense of fatness.

clue.text: Unnamed environmentalist, old rocker given welcome

indicators.note: unnamed means without N, the abbreviation for name

parts.note: a Green is an environmental campaigner
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s rock and roll fan

explanation.surface: An anonymous eco-campaigner and an ageing rock fan received a warm reception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unnamed' drops the N from GREEN, leaving GREE; Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian dress who followed rock and roll.
explanation.definitionFit: To be greeted is to be given a welcome on arrival.

clue.text: Clumsy students from e.g. Durham taking road south

parts.note: Durham is in the north-east of England, NE

explanation.surface: Awkward undergraduates from a northern university take the road south.
explanation.walkthrough: County Durham lies in North East England, hence NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Socially awkward, studious people are informally called this.

clue.text: One in a part, kind for learner to follow

definitions.note: the definition reads as (someone) for a learner to follow, with 'One' opening the clue

parts.note: a role is a part played by an actor
a model is a kind or type, as in a car model

explanation.surface: An actor in a part, a good sort for a novice to copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' and 'for learner to follow' frame the definition: someone a learner imitates; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A person whose behaviour others copy is an exemplar for a beginner to follow.

clue.text: Drunk on ship when entertaining the French

indicators.note: entertaining means holding a guest, so the French article goes inside

parts.note: on and leg are both names for the same side of a cricket field
SS stands for steamship
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Intoxicated aboard a vessel while hosting French guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' looks like a link word, but in cricket the leg side is also called the on side; the ship comes after it and 'entertaining' hosts the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Legless is British slang for so drunk one cannot stand up.

clue.text: Spot decapitated snake by country house

indicators.note: decapitated means the head of the word is cut off, so the first letter goes

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
a lodge is a house in the country, such as a hunting lodge

explanation.surface: A snake with its head chopped off lies beside a rural mansion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' means beside here, so it only places the pieces next to each other.
explanation.definitionFit: A blot or smudge of colour on a surface is a spot.

clue.text: Gunfighter gets to carry something to muffle sound

parts.note: Wyatt Earp was the famous Wild West gunfighter of the OK Corral
to lug is to carry something heavy

explanation.surface: A Wild West gunman has to carry a sound-deadening device.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug worn in the ear blocks out noise, which is muffling sound.

clue.text: Prohibition is international, an order with little right in it

indicators.note: in means the little right is placed inside the order

parts.note: an edict is an order or decree
R is the short form of right

explanation.surface: A ban described as global, an order with a small right included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in it' puts R inside EDICT to give ERDICT; 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal ban or prohibiting decree is an interdiction, as in a Scottish court's interdict.

clue.text: Thus mademoiselle is given a French flower

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
Mme abbreviates madame, the French form of address the setter meant

explanation.surface: A young French woman is presented with a bloom from France.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter wrote mademoiselle where the wordplay needs madame (MME); mademoiselle would be MLLE. 'flower' is a crossword pun on something that flows, a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower is a crossword pun for a river, something that flows, and this river runs through northern France.

clue.text: Ruler's office, for example, in which gin is kept

indicators.note: is kept, with in which, says the gin is held within the phrase for example

parts.note: say means for example, as in 'a fruit, say, an apple'
a gin is a snare or trap for animals

explanation.surface: An official's office, say, where a bottle of gin is kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' is not the drink but a snare; it sits inside SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was a provincial governor in ancient Persia, and his province or office is the satrapy.

clue.text: Mistake in swirling mist may bring state of fear

indicators.note: in places the mistake inside the rearranged mist
swirling means the letters of the word mist are whirled into a new order

parts.note: an error is a mistake

explanation.surface: A blunder in thick fog may cause panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' makes TISM from the mist, and 'in' splits that after its first letter to hold the mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Violence designed to intimidate creates a climate of fear, a reign of terror.

clue.text: Mocks some Parisian across the course of journey

indicators.note: across means the French word stretches over the journey, holding it inside

parts.note: des is French for some, as a Parisian would say it
a ride is a journey on horseback or in a vehicle

explanation.surface: Some French people make fun of a route across a course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some Parisian' is French for some, DES; it goes 'across the course of' RIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To deride someone is to ridicule them, which is mocking them.

clue.text: Progressive class, one restricted by all the others

indicators.note: restricted by means the class and one are hemmed in by all the others

parts.note: the rest means all the others
a form is a school class
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A forward-looking school class, one kept in check by the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Progressive' looks like an adjective describing the class, but it is the definition, used as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who favours gradual reform is a progressive in politics.

clue.text: Joke about female being educated prig?

indicators.note: about means the joke goes round the female

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words
Educating Rita is the Willy Russell play and film, so Rita is the female being educated

explanation.surface: A gag about a woman at school who is a self-righteous prude?
explanation.walkthrough: Educating Rita is a British play and film about a hairdresser studying literature; the question mark flags that a prig is only loosely a puritan.
explanation.definitionFit: A prig is a smugly moral person, much like a strict puritan disapproving of pleasure.

clue.text: Academic female, top lady becoming tender

parts.note: prof is short for professor, an academic
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen, the top lady

explanation.surface: A female professor who becomes the senior woman and grows gentle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb to offer.
explanation.definitionFit: To tender something is to offer it formally, as one tenders a resignation.

clue.text: Downfall of little girl English blokes upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the run of pieces upside down, reading them backwards

parts.note: sis is short for sister, a little girl
men are blokes

explanation.surface: A small girl's undoing as some Englishmen are upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses SIS + E + MEN as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A nemesis is an agent of retribution and so someone's downfall or ruin.

clue.text: Man doubled up having taken a plant for fodder

indicators.note: doubled up means the name is written twice in a row

parts.note: Alf is a man's name, short for Alfred

explanation.surface: A fellow bent double, having eaten a plant fit for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucerne, a leguminous crop, is grown as feed for livestock and called by this name in America.

clue.text: Spear, say, used in short attack

indicators.note: used in means the abbreviation for say is placed inside the attack
short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to assail is to attack
eg, exempli gratia, means for example, say

explanation.surface: A spear, for example, used in a brief assault.
explanation.walkthrough: An assegai is a Zulu weapon, so 'Spear, say' reads as an example; but 'say' is the wordplay's EG and 'short' drops a final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender iron-tipped spear used by southern African peoples such as the Zulus.

clue.text: Hunter in exploit over a very long period

parts.note: an act is a deed or exploit
an eon is an immensely long period

explanation.surface: A hunter engaged in an exploit lasting ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunter' is the mythological one: in Greek myth he saw Artemis bathing and was turned into a stag.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this huntsman was changed into a stag and killed by his own hounds.

clue.text: Old region offers bracing air, loosely speaking

parts.note: a zone is a region or area

explanation.surface: An ancient area promises fresh air, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loosely speaking' marks the definition as a colloquial use: seaside air is popularly called this, though chemically it is not.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh seaside air is popularly but inaccurately called by the name of this form of oxygen.

clue.text: Bird plunging into sea, gleefully

indicators.note: plunging into means the answer dives into the words that follow

explanation.surface: A bird dives joyfully into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'sea, gleefully'.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bird of prey with a hooked beak and broad wings.

clue.text: Son about to get covered in mud, little creature who is wicked?

indicators.note: covered in means son and about are placed inside the mud

parts.note: mire is deep mud
C is circa, Latin for about
an ant is a small creature

explanation.surface: A boy about to get muddy, a little imp who is naughty?
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered in' puts S and C inside MIRE to make MISCRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscreant is a villain, one who does wrong; 'who is wicked' describes such a person.

clue.text: A need to give an old-fashioned expression of regret

parts.note: lack means need or want

explanation.surface: A want that leads to an outdated sigh of sorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic exclamation of sorrow, as in 'alas and alack'.

clue.text: Borders that may come down close to bridges?

definitions.text: Borders that may come down close to bridges?

parts.words: Borders that may come down close to bridges?
parts.note: the bridges are not river crossings but the bridges of noses, near which a hairstyle's front edge hangs

explanation.walkthrough: Bridges suggests rivers, but it is the bridge of the nose: hair cut straight across the forehead falls close to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Edges or borders of fabric, and also hair cut to hang over the forehead, both share this name.

clue.text: Contorted expression of unhappy star

parts.note: grim means gloomy or unhappy
an ace is a star performer

explanation.surface: A twisted look on the face of a gloomy celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: A twisted face showing pain or disgust is a facial contortion.

clue.text: Bottom golfer jousts with relations, one of little stature

parts.note: the rump is the bottom or backside
Ernie Els is a South African golfer
to tilt is to joust with a lance
kin are relations

explanation.surface: The worst golfer at the tournament jousts with his family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom' looks like 'lowest-ranked', but it is the rump.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy-tale imp who spun straw into gold was a tiny man, a creature of small height.
